domain_label: Movie Studio Director — Brief-to-Shot-List Pipeline with Transition-First Planning
purpose: A method for the direction work that turns a creative brief into a locked, generation-ready shot list for stitched 3-6 s vertical reels: concept intake, beat sheet, transition-first seam planning that fixes the END frame of clip N and the START frame of clip N+1 before any generation, complete shot cards (intent, shot size, camera move, lighting, model pick, aspect ratio, duration, transition frame constraints, persona and wardrobe refs), designing around the known-hard shot list, and scene continuity across clips — with every Higgsfield model name, parameter and duration quoted only from the live MCP surface enumeration and every physics or artifact claim carried at its research-file honesty tag.
assumptions: no generation runs have happened yet; all scores are heuristic priors and every credit-cost figure is a named [UNKNOWN] to be preflighted with get_cost:true in the run phase

every Higgsfield model id, parameter, duration range, aspect-ratio set and media role comes from the read-only live MCP surface enumeration of 2026-07-03 (higgsfield_surface.md); nothing is quoted from marketing memory, and the MCP catalog is authoritative over web pages that name absent models

the known-hard shot list and physics failure rates come from the realism research file with their tags intact: eating/drinking and dexterous hand-object work are documented open problems [FACT], VideoPhy best-model physics adherence 39.6% and VideoPhy-2 hard-subset 22% are fetched abstract figures [FACT], the crowds entry is an [ESTIMATE] from taxonomy categories

transition definitions (match cut, whip pan, masked wipe, invisible cut) are canonical craft corroborated by multiple search excerpts; the flash-cut entry is convention-grade [ESTIMATE] carried as such
the output format is 9:16 1080x1920 stitched reels of 3-6 s clips; safe-zone pixel figures are practitioner ranges, not an official Meta spec (held one notch down)
exclusions: prompt-text engineering per model and the artifact-mitigation QC rubric internals (owned by the prompting/QC specialist; this KB only places the QC gates in the pipeline)
timeline execution of transitions, color grading and cover selection (editor specialist); this KB ends where the locked shot list and paired keyframes hand off
posting cadence, trial reels, analytics and platform policy (media-manager specialist)
music/soundtrack sourcing and J/L-cut audio construction beyond noting seams should plan a sound bridge
any guidance for evoking a specific real person's likeness while concealing or avoiding the face — this lane is deliberately closed and stays closed
inventing credit costs, rate limits, engagement statistics or model capabilities the MCP surface enumeration did not carry

competency_questions.question: How does a creative brief become a beat sheet, and how many shots does a 15 s or 30 s stitched reel actually carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BRIEF_CONCEPT_INTAKE states the intake fields (genre register, personas, location, the not-look-AI floor) and BEAT_SHEET_PACING gives the arithmetic: 3-6 s clips mean a 15 s reel is 3-5 shots and a 30 s reel 6-9, with the strongest image first because up to ~50% of viewers drop off in the first 3 seconds

competency_questions.question: What does transition-first planning mean, and what exactly is fixed before any video generation happens?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that the transition is chosen per seam FIRST and that it dictates the END-frame spec of clip N and the START-frame spec of clip N+1, so a stitched reel's shot list is really a transition list and both boundary frames are designed as stills before any clip is generated

competency_questions.question: What fields must every shot card carry before it is generation-ready?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: enumerates intent, shot size, camera move (one main move + speed modifier), lighting recipe, model pick, aspect ratio, duration, transition-in and transition-out frame constraints, and persona/wardrobe refs, and states a card with any empty field is not generation-ready

competency_questions.question: What END/START frame constraints does each transition type impose on the two clips it joins?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives per-type pairs: match cut (same dominant shape/position), match-on-action (same motion mid-arc and pose), whip pan (same-direction blur out/in), masked wipe (frame fully occluded both sides), invisible cut (near-identical low-detail frames), flash cut (near-white/black boundary), jump cut (identical framing, changed content), and notes whip/wipe are the most forgiving for AI mismatch

competency_questions.question: What is the known-hard shot list and how does a director design around each entry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: lists eating/drinking to the mouth, dexterous hand-object work, athletic full-body action, feet-prominent walking, legible text/badges, mirrors showing the subject, crowds/extras, and hero liquid pours held long, with the imply-not-show workarounds (glass already full, feet out of frame, reflections defocused, logo-free styling) and the honesty tags each entry carries

competency_questions.question: Which Higgsfield models accept BOTH start_image and end_image, and which are start-only or neither?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names the both-frames set (cinematic_studio_3_0, cinematic_studio_video_v2, cinematic_studio_video, seedance_2_0, seedance_2_0_mini, seedance1_5, kling3_0, minimax_hailuo, veo3_1_lite, wan2_7, marketing_studio_video), the start-only set (kling2_6, kling3_0_turbo, veo3, veo3_1, grok_video, grok_video_v15) and the neither set (gemini_omni, wan2_6), all as live-surface facts

competency_questions.question: How do per-model duration bands constrain 3-6 s clip planning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that every both-frames model covers the 3-6 s band except seedance1_5 (min 4), minimax_hailuo (min 6) and marketing_studio_video (min 12), that wan2_7 is the only model reaching 2-3 s natively, and that unsupported durations are clamped to the nearest allowed value so the beat math must be checked against the band

competency_questions.question: How is a 9:16 frame composed for reels, and when is generate-wide-then-reframe the fallback?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives the 1080x1920 canvas, the safe-zone pattern (bottom ~20%, right ~10%, top ~15% covered by UI; practitioner ranges, not Meta-official), centered composition over horizontal thirds, eyes in the upper third with ~8-12% headroom, and names the reframe tool as fallback with native 9:16 preferred

competency_questions.question: How are the camera move and lighting written onto a shot card so a video model actually carries them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAMERA_MOVE_ASSIGNMENT states one main move per shot with a speed modifier, that no Higgsfield model exposes a camera-move enum so the move lives in prompt text, presets, cinematic-studio genre/speedramp or motion_control; LIGHTING_RECIPE_ASSIGNMENT states lighting is the most impactful prompt lever (per the Veo guidance) and every light must be motivated by an in-world source

competency_questions.question: How are persona and wardrobe refs bound to shots, given the one-Soul-per-generation limit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: contrasts trained Souls (5-20 images, ~10 min, usable only with soul_2/soul_cinematic, ONE soul_id per generation) against instant Reference Elements (<<<element_id>>> placeholders, multiple per prompt, the designated path for two-persona shots), and states wardrobe/props ride as Elements while the element-compatible video-model list is partly [UNKNOWN]

competency_questions.question: Why are seam keyframes generated and QC'd as stills before any video credits are spent, and how are approved clips chained?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KEYFRAME_STILLS_FIRST states stills are the cheap place to fail and lock identity/wardrobe/lighting at t=0; START_FRAME_QC_GATE applies the worst-artifact gate (any single glance-visible artifact means re-roll) at the still checkpoint; CLIP_CHAINING_STITCH states clip N's end frame feeds clip N+1's start via media value accepting a prior job_id

competency_questions.question: What conditions must hold before the shot list locks, and how is continuity held across clips?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCENE_CONTINUITY_LEDGER states the per-scene record (wardrobe state, light direction, time of day, persona refs, grade family) that every card must match; SHOT_LIST_LOCK_VERDICT conditions the lock on every seam having a paired frame spec, every card complete, hard-shot scrub done, model/duration verified and costs preflighted

competency_questions.question: How does shot-size sequencing shape a 5-shot luxury reel?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives the size ladder (EWS to ECU), the wide/medium/close alternation rhythm, the 5-shot skeleton (detail hook, wide establish, medium in motion, second detail/reaction, wide or loop-back), Murch's emotion-first cut priority, and the eye-trace rule that the next shot's subject sits where the eye was left

competency_questions.question: How is the model pick per shot decided and A/B tested without burning the budget blind?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODEL_PICK_AB_POLICY states physics adherence varies hugely across models so shot-types are A/B'd with a per-model failure ledger, with seam clips restricted to both-frames models; CREDIT_PREFLIGHT_BUDGET states per-generation credit costs are [UNKNOWN] on the surface and must be preflighted per model-resolution-duration cell with get_cost:true before batches

glossary.definition: The atomic planning record for one 3-6 s clip: intent (the one feeling/beat it delivers), shot size, one camera move with speed modifier, lighting recipe, model pick, aspect ratio, duration, transition-in and transition-out frame constraints, and persona/wardrobe refs. A card with any empty field is not generation-ready.

The pipeline inversion for AI stitched reels: because match cuts and invisible cuts must exploit what is already in the shots, the transition is chosen per seam FIRST and dictates the last-frame spec of clip N and the first-frame spec of clip N+1 — both promptable directly via start/end-frame conditioning [craft law FACT via StudioBinder excerpts; the inversion is the research file's high-confidence design consequence].

The two designed stills that bracket one cut: clip N's END keyframe and clip N+1's START keyframe, authored as a matched pair per the chosen transition (same shape/position for a match cut, same-direction blur for a whip, full occlusion for a masked wipe) and QC'd before any video generation.

The eight shot categories current video models demonstrably fail: eating/drinking to the mouth, dexterous hand-object manipulation, athletic full-body action, feet-prominent walking, legible text/badges, mirrors showing the subject, crowds/extras, hero liquid pours [FACT/ESTIMATE tags per entry in realism_antiai.md]. Directors design around them: imply, crop, blur, or restage.

Video generation constrained by an uploaded start image and end image; the model synthesizes the motion path between them. On the live Higgsfield surface eleven models accept both roles; submitting the same image as both ends yields a loop [FACT — MCP surface + Kling excerpt].

Higgsfield's two identity mechanisms: a Soul is a trained character model (5-20 reference images, ~10 min, usable only with soul_2/soul_cinematic, ONE soul_id per generation) for solo hero fidelity; a Reference Element is an instant reusable character/environment/prop embedded as <<<element_id>>> placeholders, multiple per prompt — the designated path for two-persona shots [FACT — live tool schemas].

The craft rule for AI generation that each clip carries a single named camera move with a speed modifier (e.g. 'slow dolly in'); multi-move prompts degrade coherence in current video models [FACT-1src — Kling prompting guidance, corroborated by Runway structure advice].

UI-covered regions of the 1080x1920 reel canvas — roughly the bottom ~20% (caption/actions), right ~10% (button stack), top ~15% (branding); critical content lives in the centered core with eyes in the upper third and ~8-12% headroom. Practitioner ranges, not an official Meta pixel spec [held one notch down].

The QC doctrine that a single glance-visible artifact (garbled logo, six fingers, sliding feet) flips perceived authenticity permanently for a repeat audience, so gating is per-shot and worst-artifact-driven, not average-quality-driven: any single rubric score of 2 forces a re-roll.

The per-scene record the director maintains across clips: wardrobe state per persona, light direction and time of day, location, persona/wardrobe ref ids, and grade family — every new shot card is written against it so stitched clips read as one photographed scene.

nodes.definition: Turn the owner's brief into a working concept the whole pipeline reasons against: the genre register (classic-luxurious restraint, not new-money loud), the two personas and their world, the location palette, the format contract (9:16 stitched reels of 3-6 s clips), and the ranked #1 requirement that output must not look AI — which at intake becomes a standing constraint on every downstream choice (motivated lighting only, one living micro-detail per shot, hard-shot categories flagged before they reach a beat sheet). Intake also fixes what the concept must NOT ask for: no legible brand badges, no real-person likeness evocation (closed lane), no shots the platform surface cannot deliver.

included: the not-look-AI floor as a standing intake constraint

pros.claim: A fixed register and format contract at intake prevents every later stage from re-litigating what the reel is
pros.example: rejecting a neon-party beat at intake because the classic-luxurious register was fixed, instead of discovering the mismatch after generation

cons.claim: Over-tight intake can freeze a concept before the platform's actual strengths (presets, genre modes) are known
cons.example: locking a concept around a continuous crowd scene before learning crowds sit on the known-hard list

failure_modes: accepting a brief whose hero moments are all on the known-hard shot list
letting the not-look-AI requirement live as a vague wish instead of named constraints
acceptance_tests: the concept note states register, personas, locations, the 9:16/3-6 s format contract, and the not-look-AI constraints as named rules
revisit_triggers: the owner changes register, personas or format
the platform surface re-enumeration changes what is deliverable

base.update_signal: an owner brief change or a platform capability change moves the intake constraints

nodes.definition: Author the beat sheet with the pacing arithmetic of the format: 3-6 s clips mean a 15 s reel carries 3-5 shots and a 30 s reel 6-9 [FACT — arithmetic on the stated clip lengths]. Retention economics front-load the sheet: up to ~50% of viewers drop off within the first 3 seconds and watch-time is the dominant ranking signal [FACT/excerpt — creator-analytics guides], so the single strongest image goes FIRST with no logo/intro frame. Modulate shot length rather than cutting at a metronome: hold the hero reveal longest (4-6 s), use 2-3 s connective shots, accelerate clip lengths toward a drop [ESTIMATE — standard editorial craft, high confidence]. Each beat names its intent (one feeling), its scene, and whether it is a hero or connective clip — that intent later becomes the first field of the shot card.

pros.claim: Doing the shot-count math up front sizes the whole generation budget before a single card is written
pros.example: a 30 s reel resolving to 8 beats means 8 clips, 9 keyframe pairs including the loop seam, and a bounded credit plan

cons.claim: A beat sheet tuned purely to retention math can flatten the luxury register into generic hook-bait
cons.example: opening on a loud pattern interrupt that clashes with the quiet-luxury restraint the register demands

failure_modes: writing beats whose count does not divide into the reel length at 3-6 s per clip
burying the strongest image mid-reel
acceptance_tests: the beat sheet's clip count times its durations sums to the reel length, the strongest image is beat 1, and every beat names one intent
revisit_triggers: retention data shows a weak 3-second hold
the reel target length changes

base.update_signal: retention analytics or a format change alters the pacing math

nodes.definition: Apply the central inversion of AI stitched-reel direction: because match cuts and invisible cuts must exploit what is already present in the shots [FACT — StudioBinder match-cut/transition excerpts], and because start/end-frame conditioning makes both boundary frames directly promptable [FACT — eleven both-frames models on the live MCP surface], the transition at each seam is chosen FIRST and it dictates the END-frame spec of clip N and the START-frame spec of clip N+1 before any generation happens. A stitched reel's shot list is therefore really a transition list: N clips imply N-1 seams (N if the reel loops), and each seam's paired frame constraints are written INTO the keyframe still prompts. Nothing is generated for a clip whose two boundary frames are not yet specified.

excluded: timeline execution of the cut (editor specialist)

pros.claim: Fixing both boundary frames before generation converts editing problems into cheap still-image problems
pros.example: a whip seam specified as matching blur-out/blur-in stills, so the editor inherits a cut that already works instead of hunting for one

cons.claim: Transition-first rigidity can waste a serendipitously strong take whose boundary frames serve no planned seam
cons.example: discarding a beautiful clip because its end frame cannot pair with the next clip's locked start frame

failure_modes: generating clips first and hoping cuts can be found later
planning seams without counting the loop seam of a looping reel
acceptance_tests: every seam in the plan names its transition type and both boundary frame specs before any video generation is scheduled
revisit_triggers: a seam type proves consistently ungeneratable and the seam inventory needs rebalancing
a new both-frames model changes what seams are feasible

base.update_signal: generation runs showing seam success/failure rates per transition type recalibrate the rule's application

nodes.definition: Define the shot card, the atomic contract between direction and generation. Fields: intent (the ONE feeling/beat, per Murch's emotion-first priority), shot size (from the standard ladder), camera move (exactly one main move + a speed modifier), lighting recipe (motivated, from the lighting grammar), model pick (id from the live catalog), aspect ratio (from that model's declared set), duration (inside that model's band), transition-in frame constraint, transition-out frame constraint, and persona/wardrobe refs (soul_id or <<<element_id>>> list). A card with any empty field is not generation-ready; a card whose model/aspect/duration triple contradicts the surface catalog is invalid by construction. The card is the unit everything downstream QCs against.

included: the card as the QC reference
excluded: how each field's value is chosen (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A complete card schema makes every generation reproducible and every QC failure attributable to a field
pros.example: tracing a wardrobe mismatch to a card that omitted the wardrobe Element ref rather than to model randomness

cons.claim: Ten mandatory fields add authoring overhead that tempts shortcuts on connective shots
cons.example: leaving transition constraints blank on a 2-3 s connective clip and paying for it at the stitch

failure_modes: cards that name a model but an aspect ratio the model does not declare
cards carrying two camera moves
cards with empty transition constraints treated as generation-ready
acceptance_tests: every card lists all ten fields non-empty and the model/aspect/duration triple matches the live-surface catalog row for that model
revisit_triggers: the surface catalog changes a model's parameters or ratios
a recurring QC failure class suggests a missing card field

base.update_signal: a catalog change or a new recurring failure class changes the schema

nodes.definition: Specify the paired frame constraints per transition type [definitions FACT via StudioBinder/craft excerpts; the AI-pipeline operationalization is the research file's high-confidence mapping]. Match cut: subject A's dominant shape at position X in N's end frame; subject B of the same shape/size/position in N+1's start frame (watch face to sun, pool to champagne glass rim). Match-on-action: a motion clearly mid-arc at N's end; the SAME motion continuing from the matching pose at N+1's start. Whip pan: last ~0.3 s of N is a fast same-direction pan into full blur; N+1 opens decelerating out of matching blur — the most forgiving seam because blur hides mismatch. Masked wipe: something large sweeps across and fully fills N's final frame; N+1 starts fully blocked by a similar surface that clears. Invisible cut: near-identical low-detail boundary frames (black, blur, flat texture). Flash cut: boundary near-white or near-black [ESTIMATE — convention-grade, on-genre via paparazzi flash]. Jump cut: identical framing, changed pose/outfit. All pairs share the same lighting recipe, lens language and grade target, with boundary luminance/hue in a tight window.

included: the forgiveness ordering (whip/wipe most tolerant, graphic match strictest)
shared lighting/lens/grade requirements on the pair
excluded: editor-side blur faking and mask keyframing (editor specialist)

pros.claim: Written per-type constraints turn 'make it cut well' into checkable still-image specs
pros.example: a match-cut seam QC'd by overlaying the two keyframes and checking the round shape's screen position matches

cons.claim: Exact graphic matches are the hardest pairs for stochastic generation to hit, inviting expensive retry loops
cons.example: ten re-rolls chasing a watch-face-to-sun alignment a whip seam would have delivered in one

failure_modes: specifying whip directions that do not match across the seam
graphic-match pairs authored with different lens or lighting so the match reads as a mistake
acceptance_tests: each seam's spec names the transition type and states both frame constraints in checkable geometric/motion terms (shape, position, vector, occlusion, luminance)
revisit_triggers: seam QC shows a transition type failing repeatedly
a model's boundary-frame adherence changes the forgiveness ordering

base.update_signal: observed per-type seam success rates recalibrate the constraint table

nodes.definition: Scrub every beat against the known-hard shot list before cards are written, honesty tags intact: (1) eating/drinking to the mouth [FACT — documented failure]; (2) dexterous hand-object manipulation — pouring, typing, clasping jewelry [FACT — open research problem]; (3) athletic/gymnastic full-body action [FACT]; (4) walking/running with feet prominent in frame — foot-slide exposure [FACT — contact-point tell]; (5) legible text, signage, badges, watch-face close-ups [FACT — text tell]; (6) mirrors/large reflective surfaces showing the subject [FACT — reflection forensics]; (7) crowds and background extras [ESTIMATE — from taxonomy categories, high confidence]; (8) hero fluid shots held long [FACT — fluid classes fail; best model physics adherence 39.6% on VideoPhy, 22% on VideoPhy-2 hard subset]. Workarounds are design moves, not fixes: imply rather than show — glass already full and lifted toward lips off-frame, feet out of frame, wheels in motion blur, reflections defocused via shallow DOF, logo-free styling [ESTIMATE — direct design consequence, high confidence].

excluded: the artifact taxonomy and detection numbers behind the list (QC specialist)

pros.claim: Scrubbing at the beat level costs a rewrite of words instead of a rewrite of generated clips
pros.example: changing 'she sips champagne' to 'she lifts the full glass, cut on the smile' before any credits are spent

cons.claim: Designing around every hard category can drain the physical humanity that sells the luxury fantasy
cons.example: a reel where no one ever touches, pours or eats anything reading as sterile

failure_modes: treating the list as a prompt-engineering problem instead of a shot-design problem
letting a hero beat require a mirror reveal of the persona
acceptance_tests: every beat is annotated pass/redesigned against all eight entries, and each redesigned beat names its imply-not-show move
revisit_triggers: a benchmark or run-phase evidence shows a category improving enough to reopen
a new hard category emerges from the failure ledger

base.update_signal: physics-benchmark or run-ledger evidence that a hard category improved or a new one appeared

nodes.definition: Constrain the card's model-pick field by end-frame support, read only from the live MCP surface [all FACT, declared medias[].roles, 2026-07-03]. BOTH start_image AND end_image: cinematic_studio_3_0 (4-15 s, up to 4K, genre control), cinematic_studio_video_v2 (3-12 s, speedramp/multi-shot/cfg_scale), cinematic_studio_video (5/10 s), seedance_2_0 (4-15 s, the only model with start/end/image/video/audio reference roles), seedance_2_0_mini (4-15 s, <=720p), seedance1_5 (4/8/12 s), kling3_0 (3-15 s, std/pro/4k), minimax_hailuo (6/10 s; resolution 512 incompatible with end_image), veo3_1_lite (4/6/8 s, audio off by default), wan2_7 (2-15 s, audio_references), marketing_studio_video (12-15 s). Start-only: kling2_6, kling3_0_turbo, veo3, veo3_1, grok_video, grok_video_v15. Neither (reference-driven): gemini_omni, wan2_6. Consequence: every seam-bracketing clip MUST use a both-frames model; start-only models (including ultra-real veo3_1) are eligible only where the outgoing boundary is free.

included: the three eligibility sets verbatim from the surface

pros.claim: Eligibility read from declared media roles makes the model-pick field mechanically checkable
pros.example: rejecting a card that assigns veo3_1 to a clip whose end frame brackets a match-cut seam

cons.claim: Restricting seams to both-frames models excludes some of the strongest single-frame models from most slots
cons.example: veo3_1's ultra-real quality unusable on any clip that must land on a specified end frame

failure_modes: assigning a start-only model to a seam-bracketing clip
quoting a model's roles from marketing memory instead of the enumerated surface
acceptance_tests: the analysis reproduces the both-frames/start-only/neither sets exactly as enumerated and applies the seam rule to at least one card
revisit_triggers: a surface re-enumeration changes any model's media roles
a new model appears in the catalog

base.update_signal: any change in declared media roles on the re-enumerated surface

nodes.definition: Check every card's duration against its model's declared band [FACT — live surface duration fields]: within the both-frames set, every model covers the 3-6 s stitched-reel band EXCEPT seedance1_5 (choices 4/8/12, min 4), minimax_hailuo (6 or 10, min 6) and marketing_studio_video (min 12). wan2_7 (2-15 s) is the only model natively reaching 2-3 s. cinematic_studio_video v1 offers only 5 or 10 s; cinematic_studio_video_v2 spans 3-12 s; cinematic_studio_3_0, seedance_2_0 and seedance_2_0_mini span 4-15 s; kling3_0 spans 3-15 s. The generate envelope clamps unsupported durations to the nearest allowed value [FACT — generate_video schema], so an unchecked 3 s card on seedance1_5 silently becomes 4 s and breaks the beat math. Short clips are also protective: temporal artifacts accumulate with duration [FACT — duration-dependence per Sora's stated limitation], so the 3-6 s format is itself a realism mitigation.

included: the clamping behavior and its beat-math consequence

pros.claim: Band-checking at card time prevents silent clamping from desynchronizing the reel's timing
pros.example: catching that a 3 s connective beat assigned to minimax_hailuo would render at 6 s and double the beat

cons.claim: Strict band fit narrows model choice exactly on the shortest, most numerous connective clips
cons.example: 2-3 s connective shots forcing wan2_7 regardless of its aesthetic fit

failure_modes: planning 3 s clips on min-4 or min-6 models
assuming trim-in-post is free when the clip's motion arc was generated for the clamped length
acceptance_tests: every card's duration is an allowed value of its model's band, and the 3-6 s exceptions (seedance1_5, minimax_hailuo, marketing_studio_video) are stated
revisit_triggers: a surface re-enumeration changes any duration field
run-phase evidence quantifies trim-in-post cost

base.update_signal: a duration-field change on the re-enumerated surface

nodes.definition: Compose every card for the 9:16 1080x1920 canvas [FACT/excerpt — consistent across spec guides]. Safe zones: UI overlays cover roughly the bottom ~20% (caption/action stack), right ~10% (buttons) and top ~15% (branding), leaving a usable centered core — practitioner ranges that disagree in exact pixels, NOT an official Meta spec [held one notch down; [UNKNOWN]: Meta's own current pixel numbers]. Craft consequences: centered composition beats horizontal rule-of-thirds; eyes sit in the upper third (~30-35% from top) with ~8-12% headroom; verticals favor CU/MCU and full-body singles; true wides need strong vertical anchors; two-shots stage the personas in depth rather than side-by-side; push/pull, orbit and crane do more work per pixel than lateral moves. Aspect ratio must be in the chosen model's declared set (e.g. kling3_0 offers 16:9/9:16/1:1; veo3_1 16:9/9:16) [FACT — surface]; the reframe tool exists as a generate-wide-then-reframe fallback, but native 9:16 avoids re-composition risk [FACT tool exists; preference ESTIMATE].

included: safe-zone geometry and its held-down sourcing
vertical composition rules (center, eyes, headroom, depth staging)

pros.claim: Framing for safe zones at the still stage prevents UI from beheading the composition in-feed
pros.example: keeping the persona's face in the middle 50% vertically so neither the caption stack nor feed crop covers it

cons.claim: The centered vertical grammar constrains classic horizontal luxury compositions (car profiles, coastlines)
cons.example: a car's side profile that wants 21:9 forced into a 9:16 crop that amputates the body line

failure_modes: composing on horizontal thirds so the subject sits under the button stack
assigning an aspect ratio the model does not declare
acceptance_tests: every card's composition note places critical content in the centered core with eyes upper-third, and its aspect ratio exists in the model's declared set
revisit_triggers: platform UI overlay changes shift the safe zones
run-phase reframe results quantify the fallback's quality cost

base.update_signal: a platform UI change or an official safe-zone spec becoming available

nodes.definition: Assign each card exactly ONE main camera move with a speed modifier — multi-move prompts degrade coherence in current video models [FACT-1src — Kling guidance, corroborated by Runway structure advice; Runway's own guidance mandates a speed modifier on every move]. Choose the move for its emotional read: push-in for intimacy, pull-out for reveal/closure, orbit for hero appraisal, crane for grandeur, tracking for companionship, static for quiet-luxury confidence, whip/snap-zoom for energy and seams [FACT — movement-grammar excerpts]. Carriage paths on this surface [FACT — absence and presence read across all 28 video schemas]: NO model exposes a camera-move enum, so the move is carried by (a) prompt text in industry terms, (b) the 49 presets (packaged camera+scenario moves like 2000'S PAPARAZZI, RED CARPET, ORBITAL PRESENCE), (c) cinematic_studio genre/speedramp parameters, or (d) motion_control, which transfers the motion AND camera movement of a reference video onto a character image — the strongest camera-trick replication lever. Seam-serving boundary motion (a whip-out) counts as the shot's one move.

included: the one-move rule with speed modifier
the four carriage paths on this surface
excluded: exact prompt phrasing per model (prompting specialist)

pros.claim: One named move per card keeps generated motion coherent and makes seam vectors predictable
pros.example: 'fast whip pan right' as the sole move guaranteeing the blur direction the next clip must match

cons.claim: Single-move discipline forbids the compound choreography real cinematography sometimes wants
cons.example: an arrival beat wanting crane-down-then-push that must be split into two clips and one more seam

failure_modes: stacking two moves in one card and getting incoherent motion
naming a move without a speed modifier so the model picks the pace
acceptance_tests: every card names exactly one move with a speed modifier and its carriage path (prompt, preset, genre/speedramp, or motion_control)
revisit_triggers: a model adds a native camera-move parameter
run evidence shows a model tolerating compound moves

base.update_signal: a camera-move parameter appearing on any model schema or compound-move tolerance evidence

nodes.definition: Assign each card a lighting recipe from the sourced grammar, treating lighting as the highest-leverage prompt lever — Google's Veo prompting guidance calls lighting specification the single most impactful cinematic descriptor [FACT — via excerpts]. The recipes: three-point glamour (soft key, gentle fill, warm rim) [FACT]; motivated window key for quiet-luxury interiors [FACT on definition]; low-key + warm practicals for night luxury [ESTIMATE — synthesis]; golden-hour rim (warm halo, long parallel shadows) [FACT on the light's physics]; blue-hour nocturne [FACT]; large-soft-source specular for cars and glossy product (light the reflections, not the object) [ESTIMATE — medium-high, ASC primary source excerpt-only]. Every light must be motivated by a plausible in-world source — unmotivated glow is a recognized CG/AI tell [linkage ESTIMATE, high confidence] — and single-source scenes must state the source direction so all shadows can agree with it (multiple shadow directions are a documented forensic check [FACT]). One living micro-detail (steam, curtain, hair moving) per shot keeps the frame alive.

included: the motivated-source rule and single-shadow-direction discipline

pros.claim: A named motivated recipe per card constrains shadow geometry and buys realism where prompts have most leverage
pros.example: 'low golden sun camera-left, long parallel shadows' pinning one light direction the QC can verify

cons.claim: A short recipe menu risks visual monotony across a whole account grid
cons.example: every third reel opening on the same golden-hour rim look

failure_modes: prompting mixed light sources with no stated direction, inviting multi-direction shadows
unmotivated glamour glow that reads CG
acceptance_tests: every card names a recipe, its motivating in-world source, the key direction, and one living micro-detail
revisit_triggers: QC repeatedly flags shadow-direction errors under a recipe
a new lighting-relevant parameter appears on a model

base.update_signal: QC shadow-error rates per recipe or new lighting levers on the surface

nodes.definition: Sequence the cards' shot sizes as the reel's rhythm. The ladder [FACT — StudioBinder/B&H corroborated]: EWS/ELS, WS/LS, establishing, MS, MCU, CU, ECU. Grammar: wide establishes geography, medium carries action, close-up delivers emotion; adjacent shots should differ meaningfully in size or angle to avoid accidental jump cuts [ESTIMATE — canonical craft]. A proven 5-shot luxury skeleton [ESTIMATE, medium-high]: (1) close/detail hook (watch clasp, steam, heel on marble), (2) wide establishing the place, (3) medium of persona in motion, (4) second detail or reaction close-up, (5) wide or loop-back landing the caption. Cut priority follows Murch's Rule of Six — Emotion 51%, Story 23%, Rhythm 10%, Eye-trace 7%, 2D plane 5%, 3D space 4%; sacrifice bottom-up, never emotion [FACT/excerpt — Murch]. Eye-trace applied to 3 s shots: place the next shot's subject where the previous shot left the viewer's eye, because there is no time to rescan [ESTIMATE — direct application, high confidence].

included: the size ladder and alternation rhythm
Murch priority and eye-trace at reel speed
excluded: the transition type at each seam (SEAM_FRAME_CONSTRAINTS)

pros.claim: Size alternation gives a stitched reel cinematic rhythm and prevents accidental jump-cut reads
pros.example: detail-wide-medium-detail-wide beating five consecutive mediums that read as one broken take

cons.claim: A fixed skeleton can make an account's reels structurally predictable
cons.example: every reel opening detail-then-wide until followers feel the template

failure_modes: adjacent same-size same-angle cards reading as jump cuts
sacrificing the emotional hero frame to keep rhythm
acceptance_tests: the sequenced card list alternates sizes (no adjacent same-size-same-angle pair unless a deliberate jump cut) and marks where the eye is left at each cut
revisit_triggers: retention analytics per shot position
a genre shift changing the skeleton

base.update_signal: per-position retention data or a register change

nodes.definition: Bind persona and wardrobe refs onto each card using the surface's two identity mechanisms [FACT — live tool schemas 2026-07-03]. Souls: trained identity models (name + 5-20 reference images, ~10 min, non-blocking), usable ONLY with soul_2 and soul_cinematic, and ONE soul_id per generation — a two-persona shot cannot use two Souls in one image. Reference Elements: instant reusable character/environment/prop refs embedded as <<<element_id>>> placeholders in the prompt, multiple per prompt allowed — the surface-designated path for shots containing BOTH personas; named element-compatible image models include nano_banana_2, gpt_image_2, seedream_v4_5, seedream_v5_lite, cinematic_studio_2_5, and the video list names Cinema Studio Video 2/3.0, Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0 but was truncated in transmission [UNKNOWN whether more video models are element-compatible]. Elements are NOT usable with Soul models. The working mapping [ESTIMATE — medium-high, from these constraints]: one Soul per persona for solo hero stills, PLUS one Element per persona and wardrobe/prop Elements so two-person shots and non-Soul models hold identity; soul_cast (text-only, 16:9, budget 10-500) generates persona sheets.

included: Soul constraints (5-20 imgs, ~10 min, soul_2/soul_cinematic only, one per generation)
Element mechanics (<<<element_id>>>, multiple per prompt, compatibility lists)
excluded: reference-image curation and persona-sheet art direction (character specialist)

pros.claim: Binding refs at the card level makes identity a planned input instead of a per-generation improvisation
pros.example: a two-persona terrace card carrying both persona Elements plus the evening-wardrobe Element as three placeholders

cons.claim: The dual mechanism forces bookkeeping: Souls and Elements cover disjoint model sets and cannot be mixed
cons.example: a soul_cinematic hero still whose wardrobe Element cannot be attached because Elements are unusable with Soul models

failure_modes: planning a two-Soul single image the surface forbids
assuming an unverified video model accepts Elements
cards with no ref at all, leaving identity to chance
acceptance_tests: every card with a persona names either one soul_id (solo, soul_2/soul_cinematic only) or <<<element_id>>> refs, and two-persona cards use only the Element path on a named compatible model
revisit_triggers: the element-compatible video-model list is resolved or extended
run evidence quantifies the Soul-vs-Element fidelity gap [UNKNOWN today]
a new identity mechanism appears on the surface

base.update_signal: a compatibility-list resolution or fidelity-gap measurement changes the binding mapping

nodes.definition: Maintain the per-scene continuity ledger every card is written against, because stitched clips generated in separate calls have no shared memory: wardrobe state per persona (which Element/outfit, jacket on or off), light direction and recipe (the sun cannot move camera-left to camera-right between adjacent clips — multiple shadow directions in one scene is a documented forensic tell [FACT]), time of day (golden hour cannot neighbor noon within one scene; golden hour can be as short as ~15 minutes in the real world, so a 'same evening' scene must state one fixed sun height), location and prop state, persona ref ids, and the grade family the editor will match to a hero clip [FACT/excerpt — hero-clip shot-matching practice]. Identity drift is a named cross-shot failure [FACT], so the ledger also pins the persona's reference sheet per scene. The ledger is updated after every approved generation, not just at planning.

included: the ledger fields (wardrobe, light direction, time of day, location/props, refs, grade family)
excluded: grade matching execution in the NLE (editor specialist)

pros.claim: A written ledger converts continuity from reviewer memory into a checkable diff per new card
pros.example: catching that clip 4's card says 'blazer on' while the approved clip 3 ended blazer-off

cons.claim: Ledger discipline adds friction exactly when batches are flowing fastest
cons.example: three parallel generations approved in one sitting, none logged, and the next day's cards written against stale state

failure_modes: adjacent clips with opposite key-light directions in one scene
wardrobe changing mid-scene without a jump-cut intent
ledger updated at planning but never after approvals
acceptance_tests: every card cites the ledger row it was written against, and every scene's clips share one light direction, one time of day, and consistent wardrobe state
revisit_triggers: a stitched preview shows light-direction or wardrobe mismatch
a scene is re-timed to a different hour
persona refs are retrained or replaced

base.update_signal: observed continuity breaks at the stitch recalibrate which ledger fields are load-bearing

nodes.definition: Choose the card's model by shot-type evidence, not loyalty: physics adherence varies hugely across models (VideoPhy/VideoPhy-2 spreads; best is not average) [FACT — abstracts], so A/B candidate models per shot-type and keep a per-model failure ledger from the first batches. Surface defaults to start from [FACT — generate_video guidance]: seedance_2_0 for identity, kling3_0 for multi-shot/audio/motion transfer, kling3_0_turbo for fast single-start-frame work. Cinematic parameters that carry direction: cinematic_studio_3_0/seedance genre (auto/action/horror/comedy/noir/drama/epic), cinematic_studio_video_v2 genre adds suspense/intimate/spectacle plus speedramp (auto/custom/linear/slowmo/speedup/impact), multi_shots, cfg_scale 0-1 (0.5) and a preset_id whose interoperability with the 49 presets_show ids is [UNKNOWN]. Eligibility comes first: seam clips only from the both-frames set; then duration band; then A/B within survivors. Hard-shot categories bias the pick toward models the ledger shows failing least on that category.

included: surface default picks and cinematic parameters

pros.claim: A ledger-driven pick converts stochastic model quality into accumulated evidence
pros.example: routing all water-adjacent shots away from a model the ledger shows failing pours twice as often

cons.claim: A/B breadth multiplies cost and QC load on every new shot-type
cons.example: four candidate models on every connective clip doubling the batch budget for marginal gains

failure_modes: picking on aesthetic memory instead of the ledger
A/B-ing models already ineligible by roles or band
treating one lucky generation as a model verdict
acceptance_tests: every card's model pick names its eligibility check, band check, and the ledger evidence or A/B slot justifying it
revisit_triggers: the failure ledger accumulates enough rows to rank models per shot-type
a catalog change adds or removes candidates
preset_id interoperability is resolved

base.update_signal: ledger rankings, catalog changes, or preset-interop resolution move the pick policy

nodes.definition: Generate the seam keyframe stills BEFORE any video: for each seam, produce clip N's END still and clip N+1's START still as a designed pair carrying the seam's constraints, the card's lighting recipe, lens language, vertical framing and persona refs. Stills are the cheap place to fail — image-to-video from a QC-approved start frame locks anatomy, wardrobe and identity at t=0, converting image-QC wins into video wins and shrinking identity-drift exposure [ESTIMATE — mechanism reasoning, high confidence; category cost ordering stills-cheaper-than-video FACT with exact Higgsfield prices [UNKNOWN]]. Pairs failing QC on either frame are regenerated before video generation is scheduled. The pair must match on position, brightness, color and blur direction; end-frame conditioning controls the boundary, not the path — mid-clip motion can still wander, which is why clips stay 3-6 s and motion is prompted simply [FACT/excerpt — short-segment stability guidance].

included: the stills-before-video ordering and its cost logic
excluded: the QC rubric content (START_FRAME_QC_GATE places it)

pros.claim: Failing at the still stage costs one image; failing at the video stage costs a clip plus its seam partner
pros.example: a six-finger hand caught on a start still versus discovered mid-clip after two chained generations

cons.claim: Perfect boundary stills do not guarantee the interior of the clip, so stills-first can breed false confidence
cons.example: an approved pair whose clip morphs a hand mid-motion where no keyframe constrained it

failure_modes: skipping straight to video on schedule pressure
generating pairs with mismatched lens or luminance
treating an approved pair as approval of the whole clip
acceptance_tests: every seam has two approved stills generated before its clips are queued, and each pair passes the position/brightness/color/blur-direction match check
revisit_triggers: run evidence quantifies how often approved pairs still yield failed clips
a model's boundary adherence changes the pairing tolerance

base.update_signal: pair-approval-to-clip-success conversion rates from real runs

nodes.definition: Gate every keyframe still with the worst-artifact doctrine before it becomes a video input. Rationale carried from the human-detection evidence: one-shot human detection is barely above chance overall, but a repeat audience sees dozens of clips and one blatant tell flips the account's perceived authenticity permanently — so QC is per-shot and worst-artifact-driven, not average-quality-driven [ESTIMATE — operational reading of the meta-analysis numbers, high confidence]. At the still checkpoint the director checks the glance-visible classes: text/logos/badges (most damning, binary-checkable), identity lock against the persona sheet, object count, shadow/reflection geometry (one sun means parallel shadows [FACT — forensic check]), background coherence, and skin texture last (largely laundered by platform compression [FACT — compression removes low-level cues]). Gate: any single glance-visible artifact means re-roll — re-rolling is the cheapest fix because per-seed artifacts differ run to run [ESTIMATE — standard generative practice]. The full scored rubric belongs to the QC specialist; this node fixes WHERE it bites: no still enters chaining unQC'd.

included: the worst-artifact gating doctrine and its audience rationale
excluded: the numeric rubric and detection taxonomy (QC specialist)
raw-video and post-edit checkpoints (QC specialist owns their content)

pros.claim: Worst-artifact gating spends scarce attention where a single failure is fatal to the account
pros.example: rejecting an otherwise beautiful still for one garbled badge a follower would screenshot

cons.claim: A zero-tolerance gate on stochastic output can stall a seam through many re-rolls
cons.example: five consecutive re-rolls each failing a different rubric class on the same demanding graphic-match pair

failure_modes: averaging quality across a batch instead of gating on the worst artifact
QC'ing at full resolution on a monitor instead of feed conditions
letting schedule pressure wave an almost-clean still through
acceptance_tests: every still entering video generation carries a passed gate record, and any glance-visible artifact triggered a re-roll rather than a post-fix promise
revisit_triggers: run evidence shows a check class never failing (retire it) or a new class recurring (add it)
the QC specialist's rubric weights change

base.update_signal: class-level failure rates from real batches re-weight the checkpoint

nodes.definition: Plan the reel as a chain: clip N's end frame becomes clip N+1's start frame. Structurally supported on the surface: generate_video media values accept a prior generation's job_id, not just uploaded media [FACT — generate_video schema], so an approved clip's end can seed the next call directly; alternatively both boundary frames come from the approved keyframe stills. Each chained call names its one camera move with speed modifier and its cinematic parameters per the card. Chaining discipline: only QC-approved frames enter the chain, because an undetected artifact in a chained frame propagates into every downstream clip; and the chain inherits the continuity ledger (same light direction, wardrobe state, refs) call by call. The generate envelope allows count 1-4 per call [FACT], enabling small candidate batches per link with the best take chosen before the next link generates.

pros.claim: Chaining by job_id makes frame continuity mechanical instead of re-prompted
pros.example: clip 3 starting from exactly clip 2's final frame rather than a re-generated approximation of it

cons.claim: A serial chain serializes the schedule — each link waits on the previous link's QC
cons.example: an eight-clip reel that cannot parallelize its middle clips because each start frame is upstream output

failure_modes: chaining an unQC'd frame and propagating its artifact reel-wide
breaking the chain by re-prompting a boundary instead of reusing the approved frame
batching without selecting before the next link
acceptance_tests: every chained call references an approved frame (job_id or approved still), and the chain order matches the seam plan including any loop seam
revisit_triggers: run evidence on how job_id-seeded frames differ from re-uploaded stills
a schema change to media value acceptance

base.update_signal: chained-frame fidelity evidence or a media-value schema change

nodes.definition: Treat a looping reel's restart as one more seam — the reel's LAST clip's end frame pairs with its FIRST clip's start frame. The AI-native trick: submitting the SAME image as both start and end frame of one clip produces a natural loop [FACT/excerpt — Kling documentation; the both-frames models on this surface make it directly plannable]. Loops raise rewatches and total watch time, which ranking rewards [FACT/excerpt — loop-editing guides]. Loop the sentence, not just the pixels: end mid-motion rather than on a closed gesture so the restart reads as continuation [ESTIMATE — craft, medium-high]. Fallback when frames nearly-but-not-quite match: the editor's frame-matching trim or a short dissolve, but the director's job is to make that unnecessary by planning the loop seam with the same rigor as any interior seam — it is the seam most often forgotten in the seam count.

included: the loop-as-seam framing and same-image-both-ends trick

pros.claim: Planning the loop seam like any other seam buys rewatch time for one extra keyframe pair
pros.example: a reel whose final pull-out lands on the same terrace frame the opening push-in starts from

cons.claim: Loop constraints bind the reel's two most valuable slots (open and close) to each other
cons.example: the strongest-image-first rule fighting a loop that needs the closer to match the opener

failure_modes: forgetting the loop seam in the seam count
looping on a closed gesture so the restart reads as a stutter
acceptance_tests: a looping reel's seam list includes the last-to-first seam with a paired frame spec, and the loop point is mid-motion
revisit_triggers: rewatch analytics per looping vs non-looping reel
a format change away from looping reels

base.update_signal: rewatch analytics or a format change

nodes.definition: Budget the shot list against the surface's cost mechanism, holding the honesty line: per-generation credit cost per model is [UNKNOWN] — not exposed by models_explore, presets_show or balance [FACT — absence on the read surface]; the sanctioned zero-spend probe is get_cost:true on a generate call, which returns the credit cost WITHOUT submitting [FACT — generate envelope schema]. Rate limits and queue times are likewise [UNKNOWN] (only count<=4 per call is visible). Soul training cost is [UNKNOWN] beyond '5-20 images, ~10 min'. Discipline: before any batch, preflight each model-resolution-duration cell the plan uses; price the whole shot list (clips x candidates x re-roll allowance) against the known balance (1,010 credits, plus plan, as of 2026-07-03 [FACT]); and never let an invented per-clip price into the plan — a plan priced on guessed numbers is a plan that dies mid-reel.

included: pricing the full list including re-roll allowance

pros.claim: Cell-by-cell preflight converts an unknown price surface into a priced plan at zero spend
pros.example: learning cinematic_studio_3_0 at 1080p/5 s costs N credits before committing an eight-clip chain to it

cons.claim: Preflight adds a call per cell and can lag price changes between preflight and batch
cons.example: a plan priced Monday meeting different costs in Thursday's batch run

failure_modes: planning against invented per-clip prices
pricing clips but forgetting candidate batches and re-roll allowance
ignoring that rate limits are unknown when scheduling a deadline
acceptance_tests: the budget names every model-resolution-duration cell with a preflighted cost or an explicit [UNKNOWN-until-preflight] marker, and totals include the re-roll allowance against the live balance
revisit_triggers: get_cost results arrive and replace the [UNKNOWN]s
the balance or plan changes
rate-limit behavior is observed in runs

base.update_signal: preflight results, balance changes, or observed rate limits

nodes.definition: Compose the lock verdict: the shot list is generation-ready only when (1) every seam — including the loop seam — has a named transition type and a paired END/START frame spec; (2) every card is complete on all ten fields with model/aspect/duration validated against the live catalog; (3) every beat passed the hard-shot scrub or names its imply-not-show redesign; (4) every persona-bearing card has a valid Soul-or-Element binding respecting the one-Soul limit; (5) every card cites its continuity-ledger row; (6) seam clips sit on both-frames models within their duration bands; (7) the budget is preflighted with re-roll allowance, no invented prices; and (8) keyframe stills for at least the first scene's seams are QC-approved so the chain can start. A lock with any condition waived is not a lock; the verdict names which condition blocks and routes it back to the owning node.

pros.claim: A conditioned lock prevents the classic failure of generating against a half-planned list
pros.example: withholding the lock because three connective cards still lack transition-out constraints, caught before credits burn

cons.claim: Eight hard conditions can freeze momentum on a small reel where some conditions barely apply
cons.example: a three-clip teaser held for a full continuity ledger that is one row long

failure_modes: locking with a waived condition under deadline pressure
verdicts that fail the list without naming the blocking condition and owner
acceptance_tests: the verdict evaluates all eight conditions explicitly, names any blocker with its owning node, and no generation is scheduled off an unlocked list
revisit_triggers: run-phase evidence that a condition is too strict or too loose
a new pipeline stage adds a ninth condition

base.update_signal: run-phase evidence recalibrating the lock conditions

edges.why_related: beats are authored inside the register, personas and format contract intake fixes

the card's transition-in/out fields exist because seams are planned before shots
choosing transitions first is what makes the per-type frame-constraint table actionable

the card's model-pick field is what the eligibility sets constrain

the card's aspect-ratio and composition fields are filled by the vertical framing rules
the card's single camera-move field is what the assignment rules fill
the card's lighting field is filled from the motivated recipe menu
size rhythm is sequenced over the beat order the sheet fixes
the sequencing assigns each card's shot-size field within the ladder
the card's persona/wardrobe ref field is what Soul/Element binding fills
the ledger's light-direction and time-of-day rows record the recipes cards committed to
the ledger tracks which persona/wardrobe refs each scene's clips must keep using
A/B candidates are drawn only from the role-eligible set

the keyframe stills are generated to the per-type constraints the seam table specifies
keyframe stills must already sit in safe-zone-correct 9:16 composition

the cells to preflight are exactly the model-resolution-duration combinations the pick policy selected

the lock verifies the chain order matches the seam plan before generation starts

edges.resolution_rule: the known-hard list wins: the beat is redesigned imply-not-show at the beat level; the brief's intent survives, its literal staging does not

edges.why_related: the aesthetically strongest model for a look may be start-only (veo3_1) while the seam demands end-frame support
edges.resolution_rule: eligibility wins at seams: seam-bracketing clips use both-frames models; start-only models are eligible only for clips whose outgoing boundary is free

edges.why_related: a 2-3 s connective beat collides with models whose minimum is 4, 6 or 12 seconds and with silent clamping
edges.resolution_rule: re-assign the clip to a band-covering model (wan2_7 for 2-3 s, cinematic_studio_video_v2 or kling3_0 for 3 s) or re-time the beat; never let clamping resolve it silently

edges.why_related: a seam demanding boundary motion (whip-out) competes with the one-move rule when the beat wants a different interior move
edges.resolution_rule: the seam-serving move counts as the shot's single move; if the beat's emotional move is incompatible, change the transition type at that seam rather than stacking moves

edges.why_related: A/B exploration breadth multiplies cost against a finite preflighted balance
edges.resolution_rule: budget wins: A/B breadth is capped to hero shot-types and funded from the preflighted allowance; connective clips ride the ledger's current best model

edges.why_related: the loop is a self-seam: the last-to-first restart obeys the same paired frame constraints as any interior transition
gating stills before they enter the chain causally prevents a single artifact from propagating through every downstream chained clip
drift observed at the stitch (wardrobe, light direction, identity) feeds back as ledger corrections for the next cards

conflict_axes.name: brief_ambition_vs_known_hard_list
conflict_axes.description: The luxury brief naturally wants exactly what models fail at — pours, dining, badges, mirrors, crowds — while the hard-shot list demands those beats be restaged.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: redesign at the beat level with imply-not-show moves; the intent survives, the literal staging does not

conflict_axes.name: seam_precision_vs_generation_forgiveness
conflict_axes.description: Exact graphic matches read most premium but are hardest for stochastic generation to hit, while whip pans and masked wipes hide mismatch inside blur and occlusion.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer whip and masked-wipe seams early in production; reserve exact graphic matches for hero seams once keyframe control is proven

conflict_axes.name: aesthetic_model_vs_end_frame_support
conflict_axes.description: The strongest-looking model for a shot may be start-only (veo3_1 ultra-real) while transition-first planning needs both boundary frames pinned.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: seam-bracketing clips must use the both-frames set; start-only models serve only free-boundary clips

conflict_axes.name: native_vertical_vs_wide_then_reframe
conflict_axes.description: Native 9:16 generation avoids re-composition risk but constrains composition; generating wide and reframing recovers horizontal grammar at re-crop cost.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default native 9:16; reach for reframe only when a composition genuinely needs the wide canvas and the crop is planned in advance

conflict_axes.name: beat_timing_vs_model_duration_bands
conflict_axes.description: The beat sheet's 2-3 s connective rhythm collides with models whose minimum duration is 4, 6 or 12 seconds and with silent clamping to allowed values.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the timing wins: move the clip to a band-covering model or re-time the beat explicitly; never accept a silent clamp

conflict_axes.name: exploration_breadth_vs_credit_budget
conflict_axes.description: Per-shot-type A/B across models builds the failure ledger fastest but multiplies generation cost against an unknown-priced, finite balance.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: preflight every cell with get_cost:true, cap A/B to hero shot-types, and let the ledger's current best carry connective clips

conflict_axes.name: per_shot_beauty_vs_cross_clip_continuity
conflict_axes.description: The best individual take (light, pose, energy) may contradict the scene ledger's committed wardrobe state, light direction or time of day.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: continuity wins within a scene — a gorgeous mismatched clip reads as an error at the stitch; re-roll toward the ledger

conflict_axes.name: soul_fidelity_vs_element_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: Trained Souls promise identity fidelity but bind to two image models and one Soul per generation; Elements are instant and multi-ref but their fidelity gap is unmeasured.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: Souls for solo hero stills on soul_2/soul_cinematic; Elements for two-persona shots and all non-Soul models; measure the fidelity gap in early runs (it is [UNKNOWN] today)

conflict_axes.name: single_move_coherence_vs_compound_choreography
conflict_axes.description: One move per shot keeps AI motion coherent, but cinematic beats sometimes want compound moves that must be split into extra clips and seams.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the one-move rule; express compound intent as two chained clips joined by a planned seam rather than one overloaded prompt

edge_cases.description: A two-persona shot needs both identities but the surface allows only ONE soul_id per generation
edge_cases.trigger: a card binds two Souls to one image or clip
edge_cases.mitigation: route two-persona shots through Reference Elements (multiple <<<element_id>>> placeholders) on a named element-compatible model; Souls stay for solo hero stills

edge_cases.description: A graphic-match seam's two keyframes refuse to align on shape/position after repeated re-rolls
edge_cases.trigger: several consecutive pair generations fail the overlay match check
edge_cases.mitigation: downgrade the seam to a whip or masked wipe whose blur/occlusion tolerates mismatch, and reserve the graphic match for a seam where keyframe control is proven

edge_cases.description: A 3 s connective beat is assigned to seedance1_5 (min 4 s) or minimax_hailuo (min 6 s) and the envelope silently clamps the duration
edge_cases.trigger: a card's duration is not an allowed value of its model's band
edge_cases.mitigation: band-check every card at authoring; move 2-3 s clips to wan2_7 or 3 s clips to cinematic_studio_video_v2/kling3_0, or re-time the beat explicitly

edge_cases.description: minimax_hailuo is set to resolution 512, which is incompatible with end_image conditioning (and unsupported by its 2.3 variants)
edge_cases.trigger: a hailuo seam clip is configured at 512
edge_cases.mitigation: keep hailuo seam clips at 768/1080, or move the clip to another both-frames model

edge_cases.description: The brief demands a legible marque badge or watch-face close-up — hard-list entry 5, and genre experts scrutinize exactly those objects
edge_cases.trigger: a beat requires readable text, logos or badges in frame
edge_cases.mitigation: logo-free styling, angle/DOF choices that keep lettering sub-legible, or imply the brand through silhouette and context; never ship near-miss lettering

edge_cases.description: A dressing-room or elevator beat stages the persona in front of a mirror, exposing reflection-geometry forensics
edge_cases.trigger: a large reflective surface shows the subject
edge_cases.mitigation: defocus the reflection via shallow DOF, reframe it out, or restage the beat; mirrors stay on the avoid list

edge_cases.description: An undetected artifact in an approved-looking frame is chained via job_id and propagates into every downstream clip
edge_cases.trigger: a boundary frame enters the chain without the QC gate
edge_cases.mitigation: no frame enters the chain unQC'd; on discovery, break the chain at the last clean frame and regenerate forward

edge_cases.description: Per-generation credit costs are not exposed anywhere on the read surface, so the shot list cannot be priced from documentation
edge_cases.trigger: budgeting is attempted before any get_cost preflight
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the named [UNKNOWN] and preflight each model-resolution-duration cell with get_cost:true (returns cost without submitting) before any batch

edge_cases.description: The element-compatible VIDEO model list was truncated in transmission, so two-persona video plans may target an incompatible model
edge_cases.trigger: a two-persona video card assumes Element support beyond the named Cinema Studio 2/3.0, Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the [UNKNOWN], plan two-persona video only on the named-compatible models, and verify the full list on the next surface read

edge_cases.description: cinematic_studio_video_v2 exposes a preset_id and higgsfield_preset requires one, but whether all 49 presets_show ids are valid for both routes is unstated
edge_cases.trigger: a card routes a preset through the v2 parameter assuming interoperability
edge_cases.mitigation: treat preset interop as [UNKNOWN]; use presets via higgsfield_preset as designed and test the v2 route with a single preflighted probe before relying on it

edge_cases.description: A 'same evening' scene generated across batches drifts from golden hour toward noon light between adjacent clips
edge_cases.trigger: time-of-day is described loosely and re-prompted per batch
edge_cases.mitigation: pin one sun height and key direction in the ledger row and copy it verbatim into every card of the scene; QC adjacent boundary frames for light agreement

edge_cases.description: A looping reel is planned with N-1 seams, forgetting that the restart is itself a seam
edge_cases.trigger: the seam list omits the last-to-first pair
edge_cases.mitigation: count seams as N for a looping reel and give the loop seam a paired frame spec like any interior seam

workflow.action: Fix the concept: register, personas, format contract, not-look-AI constraints
workflow.description: Turn the brief into named constraints including the closed likeness lane and the 9:16/3-6 s contract
workflow.gate: register, personas, format and the standing constraints are stated as rules

workflow.action: Author the beat sheet with pacing math and front-loaded strongest image
workflow.description: Resolve reel length into 3-6 s beats, each with one intent, hero/connective role and modulated length
workflow.gate: durations sum to the reel length and beat 1 carries the strongest image

workflow.action: Scrub every beat against the known-hard shot list
workflow.description: Check all eight hard categories and redesign offending beats imply-not-show
workflow.artifact: scrubbed beat sheet with redesign notes
workflow.gate: every beat is annotated pass or redesigned with its workaround named

workflow.action: Choose the transition per seam and count the seams
workflow.description: Assign each seam (including the loop seam) a transition type before any card or generation exists
workflow.gate: every seam has a named type; looping reels count N seams

workflow.action: Write the paired END/START frame constraints per seam
workflow.description: Spec both boundary frames per the per-type table in checkable geometric/motion terms
workflow.gate: each spec states shape/position/vector/occlusion/luminance constraints for both frames

workflow.description: Fill all ten fields per clip: intent, size, one move + speed, lighting recipe, model, aspect, duration, both transition constraints, refs
workflow.gate: no card has an empty field or a catalog-contradicting model/aspect/duration triple

workflow.action: Validate model eligibility and duration bands per card
workflow.description: Confirm seam clips sit on both-frames models and every duration is an allowed band value
workflow.gate: no seam clip on a start-only model; no duration outside its band

workflow.action: Bind persona and wardrobe refs and open the continuity ledger
workflow.description: Assign soul_id or <<<element_id>>> refs respecting the one-Soul limit; record wardrobe, light direction and time of day per scene
workflow.gate: every persona card has a valid binding and cites a ledger row

workflow.action: Generate and QC the seam keyframe stills
workflow.description: Produce each seam's still pair, run the worst-artifact gate, re-roll failures before any video
workflow.gate: every pair passes the match check and the QC gate; no unQC'd still proceeds

workflow.action: Plan the chain and the loop
workflow.description: Order the chained generations (job_id or approved stills as boundaries), batch count<=4 candidates per link, close the loop seam
workflow.gate: chain order matches the seam plan and only approved frames enter it

workflow.action: Preflight the budget and issue the lock verdict
workflow.description: Price every model-resolution-duration cell via get_cost:true with re-roll allowance, then evaluate all eight lock conditions
workflow.gate: all eight conditions pass with no waiver, or the verdict names the blocker and its owning node

dominance_rules.rule: The known-hard shot list dominates brief ambition
dominance_rules.rationale: eating/drinking, hand-object work, feet, text, mirrors, crowds and hero pours are documented model failures; staging them literally ships tells
dominance_rules.trigger: a beat requires a hard-list category
dominance_rules.action: redesign the beat imply-not-show at the beat level before any card is written

dominance_rules.rule: Seam frame constraints dominate interior shot preference
dominance_rules.rationale: the stitched reel lives or dies at its cuts; a beautiful clip that cannot cut is a failed clip
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot's preferred framing or move contradicts its seam's boundary spec
dominance_rules.action: conform the shot to the seam spec or change the transition type; never generate against an unmet boundary

dominance_rules.rule: Both-frames eligibility dominates aesthetic model preference at seams
dominance_rules.rationale: a start-only model cannot land on a specified end frame, so the seam physically cannot be honored
dominance_rules.trigger: a seam-bracketing card names a start-only model
dominance_rules.action: reassign to the both-frames set (cinematic studio, seedance, kling3_0, hailuo>=768, veo3_1_lite, wan2_7)

dominance_rules.rationale: stills are the cheap place to fail; an artifact caught after video generation costs the clip and its seam partner
dominance_rules.trigger: a deadline tempts skipping the keyframe stage
dominance_rules.action: hold the ordering: no video call until both boundary stills pass the gate

dominance_rules.rule: The live MCP surface dominates memory and marketing claims
dominance_rules.rationale: model ids, roles, durations and ratios were enumerated with has_more:false; web pages name models (Sora, Cinema Studio 3.5) absent from this account's catalog
dominance_rules.trigger: any model name, parameter or duration is about to be quoted
dominance_rules.action: quote only the enumerated surface and treat catalog-absent names as unavailable

dominance_rules.rule: The continuity ledger dominates per-shot beauty within a scene
dominance_rules.rationale: a gorgeous take with the wrong light direction or wardrobe state reads as an error at the stitch and as an AI tell
dominance_rules.trigger: a candidate take contradicts the scene's ledger row
dominance_rules.action: re-roll toward the ledger; only the owner can re-time a scene

dominance_rules.rule: The worst-artifact gate dominates average quality
dominance_rules.rationale: a repeat audience forgives mediocrity but not one garbled badge or six-fingered hand; single tells flip perceived authenticity permanently
dominance_rules.trigger: a batch is judged by overall impression
dominance_rules.action: gate per shot on the single worst artifact; any glance-visible tell means re-roll

dominance_rules.rule: A named [UNKNOWN] dominates an invented number
dominance_rules.rationale: credit costs, rate limits, Soul training cost, the Element video list and preset interop are unexposed; plans built on guessed values fail mid-reel
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan needs a value the surface did not expose
dominance_rules.action: carry the [UNKNOWN] by name and resolve it with the sanctioned probe (get_cost:true, surface re-read), never by invention

dominance_rules.rule: Native 9:16 dominates generate-wide-then-reframe when the model declares 9:16
dominance_rules.rationale: reframe re-composition risks the safe-zone and eye-line work already done at the still stage
dominance_rules.trigger: a card considers the wide-then-reframe path
dominance_rules.action: generate native 9:16 unless the composition genuinely needs the wide canvas and the crop is planned in advance

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair and approve both seam frames before any video generation on either side of the cut
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating whole clips because their boundaries cannot cut together

anti_rework_rules.rule: Scrub beats against the hard-shot list before writing shot cards
anti_rework_rules.prevents: carding, generating and QC-failing shots that were undeliverable by category from the start

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a model's media roles and duration band on the live surface before writing it onto a card
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cards invalidated later by start-only roles or silent duration clamping

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the worst-artifact gate on keyframe stills before spending video credits
anti_rework_rules.prevents: video-stage discovery of text/hand/shadow tells that were visible in the still

anti_rework_rules.rule: Create persona Souls/Elements and wardrobe Elements before the first persona shot generates
anti_rework_rules.prevents: identity-inconsistent early clips that force reshooting the scene once refs exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pin light direction and time of day in the continuity ledger before generating a scene's second clip
anti_rework_rules.prevents: adjacent clips with contradictory sun directions that no grade can reconcile

anti_rework_rules.rule: Preflight get_cost:true per model-resolution-duration cell before batch generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: running out of credits mid-chain and stranding a half-generated reel

anti_rework_rules.rule: Count the loop seam and spec its frame pair at planning time for looping reels
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering at the edit that the reel's open and close cannot loop and regenerating one of them

iteration_protocol.trigger: a seam fails at the stitch — boundary frames mismatch or the transition reads as a jump
iteration_protocol.action: regenerate the keyframe pair to spec, or downgrade the seam to a whip/masked wipe and update the seam list

iteration_protocol.trigger: identity or wardrobe drift is observed across a scene's clips
iteration_protocol.action: re-bind the persona/wardrobe refs, correct the ledger row, and re-roll the drifted clips from approved frames

iteration_protocol.trigger: a surface re-enumeration changes model roles, durations, ratios or the catalog itself
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the eligibility sets, duration bands and pick policy, and re-validate every unlocked card

iteration_protocol.trigger: a glance-visible artifact passes a checkpoint and is caught downstream
iteration_protocol.action: break the chain at the last clean frame, re-roll forward, and add the missed class to the still-checkpoint list

iteration_protocol.trigger: get_cost preflight prices a planned cell far above the allowance
iteration_protocol.action: re-plan the pick (cheaper model, lower resolution, fewer candidates) or cut shot count, then re-price the list

iteration_protocol.trigger: the element-compatible video-model list or preset_id interoperability is resolved on a later surface read
iteration_protocol.action: replace the named [UNKNOWN]s, widen or narrow the two-persona video plan and preset routing accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: retention analytics show a weak 3-second hold on published reels
iteration_protocol.action: re-order beats to front-load the strongest image and tighten clip 1's pattern interrupt within the register

priority_rationale: Intake, beat sheet, transition-first planning and the shot-card schema come first because every downstream field is authored inside the contract they fix; the seam constraint table and hard-shot scrub follow because they reshape beats before cards harden; the platform nodes (end-frame eligibility, duration bands) then bind cards to what the enumerated surface can actually deliver; the craft-assignment nodes (framing, camera, lighting, size, refs, ledger) fill the cards; and the execution chain (stills-first, QC gate, chaining, loop, budget preflight) plus the lock verdict come last because they convert the plan into spendable, gated generation order.
